newsitem.title: CHINA: China anti-dumping laws eye colour film, steel.
newsitem.headline: China anti-dumping laws eye colour film, steel.

text.p: China said on Sunday it had received complaints of dumping of foreign colour film, plywood, asbestos, steel and household appliances on its markets.

But the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation had not formally investigated the complaints because of a lack of laws, the China Daily Business Weekly said, quoting Zhang Yuqing, a deputy director-general of the ministry.
The newspaper did not single out a country or company for dumping goods in China.
The ministry had drafted an anti-dumping bill to protect domestic exporters and submitted a draft to higher authorities for approval, it said without elaborating.
"In a world where tariff and non-tariff barriers decrease rapidly, anti-dumping measures are becoming increasingly important in protecting domestic manufacturers," Zhang was quoted as saying.
Some countries were abusing the practice and turning it into a tool for trade protectionism, he said without identifying them.
Foreign countries investigated more than 250 anti-dumping lawsuits against Chinese exports by end-1996, the newspaper said.
Chinese exporters of bicycles, televisions, fabrics, shoes and bags had been hit by anti-dumping lawsuits, it said.
Zhang defended China, saying a rising number of foreign-funded ventures in China were targets of investigation for dumping their goods abroad.
Low costs made China an easy target for unfair and discriminatory dumping charges, Zhang said.
China would continue to negotiate with other countries to change unreasonable practices, such as imposing unified anti-dumping tariffs on all Chinese exports in a certain sector, he said.
However, China would cancel the export licences of enterprises found to be dumping their goods abroad, Zhang said.
